Aggregates are count, count&#95;distinct, sum, average, minimum and maximum. Expressions are field references (nested paths included), &#95;&#95;name&#95;&#95;, literals, the six comparisons, and, or, not, xor, nor, exists, is&#95;absent, is&#95;error, type, is&#95;type, array&#95;contains, array&#95;contains&#95;all, array&#95;contains&#95;any, equal&#95;any and not&#95;equal&#95;any, array and map construction and document&#95;id / collection&#95;id / parent of a document reference. FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 to O-4 (production, Enterprise, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20) answered every comparison, construction, alias, select-width, literal, map-key, document-function, limit/offset and where-condition probe it was given as the official emulator does (every pair of kinds, vectors by length first and missing fields included; integers and doubles exactly as one kind; the select alias length limit of 1500 UTF-8 bytes on the unquoted joined path; argument checks of unrun stages in the recorded orders). Both profiles answer those alike. What production has not answered (a collection reference with a non-ASCII name; a key that is not a plain name in a literal holding an expression; document-function argument types other than string, integer, map and boolean; map keys other than integer and boolean; malformed or integer vectors; several empty or reserved literal keys and the key &#95;&#95;name&#95;&#95;; limit types other than integer and string, offsets other than a non-negative integer and a string; fireemu's own argument-count and option texts; an empty map or a later check after a function or stage value fireemu does not check; documents paths other than a collection and a document) is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED under strict and answered as the official emulator answers it under the emulator profile. A field equality is applied by the scan without index validation (Enterprise needs no index; pending production observation). A run-time refusal may follow partial results; rows after a used-up limit are not evaluated. The same subset runs over REST :executePipeline (the Web SDK Lite transport); a REST refusal answers no partial results. Without a select a result is the whole source document (name and times); every response carries the snapshot read time as executionTime. Known differences from production: the groups of an aggregate come in the order they were first met, where production's is its own and unobserved (so a limit, an offset or a sort with tied keys after the groups can differ), and a limit after a sort cuts a group of rows tied on every sort key in an order the scan order does not explain; an unsorted read is in production's scan order, ascending CRC-32 of the document IDs. A larger answer is cut into responses or array elements at about 1 MiB of results; production cuts a larger answer into units of 5 to 199 results (2 KB to 37 KB) whose boundaries differ between two reads of the same data (500 small documents came in 3 to 9 units, 5000 in 26 to 40; a document of 400 KB or more is a unit of its own and 100 KB documents come two to a unit), and put every recorded answer of 50 small documents or fewer in one response or element (FS-ENT-ORACLE O-8A); fireemu's cut differs. Offset skips filtered rows once across the existing paged stream. The stages union, unnest, sample, find&#95;nearest, replace&#95;with and the database input, the math, string, timestamp and map function families and consistency selectors remain unsupported. Production behavior is observed only as the FS-ENT-ORACLE recordings O-1 to O-9b took it (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-27: the stage grammar and its refusal texts, sort and stage order, where-context answers, aggregate, distinct, add&#95;fields, remove&#95;fields, collection&#95;group, documents, the order of a read without a sort, the string, math, timestamp, map and array function families, union, unnest, sample, is&#95;type over every type name and the response framing); the string, math, timestamp, map and array families, union, unnest and sample are recorded but not run locally. Not observed: error precedence on the Standard (default) database and for a non-owner caller, base64 decoding in createDocument, patch and batchWrite, non-ASCII document IDs and CRC-32 ties, and is&#95;type of a vector. Production answers two shapes with an HTTP 500 INTERNAL that fireemu does not reproduce: an alias repeated in quotes and array&#95;reverse() with no argument. Language tags/overrides are validated but enable no language-specific analysis; there is no stemming, synonym expansion, typo correction or automatic language detection; productionExact refuses every search with FS&#95;TEXT&#95;UNOBSERVED until corresponding production behavior is recorded; local tests and SDK wire compatibility do not attest production equivalence; Query bounds: 8192 UTF-8 bytes and 64 clauses. Only string-valued indexed fields produce postings. Real posting data is reconstructed at the query snapshot; this is not an incremental-commit performance claim; Empty or whitespace-only input, whole plain tokenless input and exclusions-only queries return no hits. Plain tokenless fragments are ignored alongside searchable terms and still count toward the clause bound; quoted or excluded tokenless fragments remain rejected. Unquoted colons delimit conjunctive terms. A leading unmatched quote leaves an ordinary conjunction, while balanced phrases remain positional within one field. OR/or is conjunctive between positive operands and searchable alone; other OR contexts remain unsupported. Legacy field-qualified quoted phrases remain unobserved development approximations, not native-compatible qualified phrase support; Local build controls are explicit; a supplied generation fences stale operations. Catalog source/progress/postings are isolated and participate in session snapshot/reset ownership and retained-byte estimates; Standard edition still accepts valid searchConfig files without serving search. Geo-only definitions remain outside the text catalog. Search definitions never satisfy an ordinary composite-index requirement; Purpose-specific Latin folding is a bounded development approximation, not a native analyzer reconstruction. Standalone combining marks and non-Latin bases remain distinct; CJK segmentation, scoring and broader Unicode behavior remain unverified. productionExact is unchanged. |
